research/agentic/DECISION_LOG.md: no row tests a BF16 cast restricted to the MLP-input norm output; CONFOUNDED rows (batch-ramp 2397, no-ngram-ve 2548, bf16-norm-output 2716) all cross the data wall by >=9%, whereas the expected +8..18% of this change is a smaller excursion
expected_effect: Steps +8% to +18% versus same-host control (2240-2445 on trn21; 2245-2450 on trn22), i.e. a substantial fraction of the +31% seen with the complete norm-output policy since the MLP is the largest linear group; public_val_bpb lower than same-host control by 0.002-0.006 (SUCCESS threshold >= 0.002). Falsified-quality if BPB >= control despite >= +3% steps; falsified-inert if steps within +/-2% of control.
hypothesis: The +31% step-rate of the complete --bf16-norm-output policy (2716 steps vs 2071 on trn21) is mostly earned at the block projection boundaries, while its fixed-budget quality regression (1.016279 vs 1.005734) is carried by the sites that policy also converts outside the blocks (final norm feeding the FP32 LM head) and by the ~24% of steps spent past the ~2195-step data wall. The isolated --bf16-sdpa-input boundary already showed a precision cast at one expensive boundary is quality-neutral-to-positive at fixed budget (2233 steps, 1.002028 vs 2076 / 1.005967). Casting ONLY the norm output that enters the MLP (the largest linear group in the block) to BF16, while leaving every other norm output, the residual stream, the final norm and the LM head in FP32, should recover a substantial fraction (+8..18%) of the global-policy speed with a much smaller data-wall excursion, and therefore lower public_val_bpb versus the same-host control.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-mlp-input-norm-only from 9a4caa7b. STEP 2 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT ('0' disables), argparse pair --bf16-mlp-norm-output / --no-bf16-mlp-norm-output (dest bf16_mlp_norm_output, default None -> constant), resolved in main() at the place where the other precision toggles (bf16_norm_output, bf16_sdpa_input) are resolved, and append 'USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT' to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (around lines 5251-5266) so current_toggles()/save_checkpoint() persist it and load_for_eval() restores it before model construction. Default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. STEP 3 (single-site cast; do NOT modify norm()): at exactly the MLP-input norm call identified in STEP 1(b) in the default serial path, bind the norm result to a local (e.g. mlp_in = norm(x)) and immediately follow it with: if USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT and mlp_in.dtype != <GLOBAL cast target>: mlp_in = mlp_in.to(<GLOBAL cast target>) -- using the identical cast target recorded in STEP 1(a); then pass mlp_in to self.mlp(...) exactly where norm(x) was passed before. If any op sits between that norm and self.mlp (e.g. a gate multiply), apply the cast immediately at the norm output and leave the intervening op untouched. If Block.forward has parallel_block or mlp_sandwich code paths with their own MLP-input norm call, apply the same three-line pattern at that one call in each path so the toggle has one consistent meaning (the default path is the one exercised by the candidate); leave the sandwich post-MLP norm and every other norm call untouched. single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: a new module-level toggle USE_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT (default True; env NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_MLP_NORM_OUTPUT='0' disables; CLI --bf16-mlp-norm-output/--no-bf16-mlp-norm-output; appended to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES so checkpoints persist it and load_for_eval restores it) casts exactly ONE tensor per transformer Block to BF16: the output of the norm(x) call whose result is the direct input of the MLP module (the argument of self.mlp(...)) in Block.forward. The cast target is identical to the one the existing --bf16-norm-output policy uses and is guarded by a dtype check so that under --bf16-norm-output (where norm already returns BF16) behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged. Acknowledged downstream propagation: the MLP up-projection/activation/down-projection run on BF16 activations via the already-exercised BF16-input Linear path, and the MLP output is added to the FP32 residual with the existing promotion semantics -- exactly the path the --bf16-norm-output full run exercised end-to-end. NOT changed: the pre-attention norm(q_in)/norm(k_in)/norm(v_in) outputs, the norm feeding local_conv, QK norms/rope_norm, the initial embedding norm in GPT.forward, the final norm before lm_head, lm_head, logits/softcap/CE, ngram-ve, optimizer, schedule, batch, data, eval, causality, launch shape or environment. num_params_M must remain 592.9 and every existing config oneliner must be identical to the control except for one added field. Launch smoke and full with the exact control command/environment and no additional flags. Full-run classification vs same-host pinned control (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967), in order: (1) HALT-INERT if static inspection finds the MLP-input norm output is already BF16 under default flags (no patch, no run); (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if full-run steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-2% of control (the MLP-input boundary is not a measurable cost); (4) SUCCESS if steps >= +3% of control and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.002; (5) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +3% and public_val_bpb >= control (BF16 at the MLP input costs more quality than the extra steps buy); (6) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise (+2..3% steps, or >= +3% with a gain smaller than 0.002). Verdicts use only fixed-budget public_val_bpb; the Analyst records as attribution notes (not verdict inputs) the fraction of steps beyond the ~2195-step data wall and the smoothed training-loss value at the control's final step count.
